prize_parts.citation: for incorporating firm heterogeneity into trade theory, showing how selection into exporting and reallocation across firms shape trade patterns and the gains from trade

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: one part, B010, credited to Helpman and Melitz. The discovery is that firms within an industry differ in productivity, and that this produces selection into exporting, reallocation of activity toward more productive firms after liberalisation, and a channel for gains from trade distinct from comparative advantage and from scale and variety. Melitz (2003) is the central model, and Helpman's work, including Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, extends it to firm boundaries and multinational activity. Representative-firm new trade theory does not generate exporter premia, the fact that only a subset of firms export, or within-industry productivity gains from entry and exit. Firm-level data across many countries have tested these predictions for more than twenty years. My reading, from my own recollection and not independently verified, is that the qualitative selection result needs only that productivity ranks which firms export, so it does not hinge on Pareto draws. The size of the welfare gains is more sensitive to the distributional assumption. A narrow citation can honour the mechanism without claiming a particular welfare number. I read the convergence of eight members on the same pair as evidence that the attribution is stable across assessors. It is not evidence of merit. My case rests on the size and durability of the contribution and on a credit structure I can defend under the three-name cap. The round-1 exchange added no new scientific argument that moves me to another part. It did sharpen the citation wording and my ranking of the alternatives.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is credit. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and Hopenhayn in firm dynamics, are precursors or parallel contributors who are not credited, and Redding's quantitative and spatial extensions are also left out. I would handle this through narrow wording and an explicit acknowledgement in the scientific background, and I accept that the handling is a judgement and not a resolution. The second reservation is that the quantitative gains from selection depend on parametric assumptions. The third is field balance after the 2008 trade prize. I do not think that should decide between candidates on merit, but I accept it as something the Committee may weigh openly. Finally, my own expertise in trade and industrial organisation gives me an obvious prior in favour of B010. The Committee should discount my judgement accordingly and check it against members from other fields, who have reached the same pair independently.

responses.point: Boppart keeps B019 (Kiyotaki and Moore) as his preferred part. He argues that it is a single mechanism with two clear originators, and that B010 has real credit disputes with Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum. He now treats B010 as a serious alternative.
responses.response: I accept that B019 has the tidier attribution of the two, and I raise it from a low opening rank to my first alternative. That is a change from round 1. I still prefer B010 on two grounds. The mechanism has been confronted with firm-level data across many countries. The collateral-amplification channel is identified more indirectly, and the 2022 prize on banks and financial crises is thematically adjacent. His credit objection to B010 is fair. But the precursor facts motivated the model and did not supply the unifying framework, and I would let the citation and background text acknowledge them. I do not think B019 is the weaker candidate on science. We weigh single-mechanism cleanliness against breadth of confirmation differently.

responses.point: Strömberg prefers B019 with Kiyotaki and Moore, narrowed from three names after discussion. He says he is not fully settled on the order of B019 and B010, and that B010 may be the safer case.
responses.response: His two-name narrowing removes the Gertler problem, which I regarded as the main weakness of the B019 attribution. It makes B019 a better fallback than I treated it in round 1. If the Committee judged B010 too close to the 2008 recognition, I would not resist B019 with the two originators. I disagree with him on one point only. I give more weight to the evidence base than to the cleanliness of the credit line, and for B010 the evidence is direct and cumulative. Since he says he is unsettled, the real difference between us may be small. It is an ordering of two strong candidates, and it would be a mistake to read it as a dispute about merit.

responses.point: Enflo prefers B032 with Autor, Hanson and Dorn. She narrowed from Katz to Dorn, and argues that the China-shock evidence on local labour-market adjustment has been stress-tested for a decade, while accepting that B010 and B019 have cleaner credit structures.
responses.response: Dropping Katz makes the attribution much more defensible, and I respect her willingness to move. I rank B032 below my two alternatives for two reasons. The ballot entry still bundles the task-framework and trade-shock strands. The long-run persistence and the shift-share identification are still debated. I agree with her that continued debate over magnitudes shows scrutiny and not fragility, and that the qualitative finding on slow regional adjustment has survived re-examination. In this field the same logic applies to B010, where the sign and mechanism are robust and the magnitudes are model-sensitive. I would keep B032 as a serious candidate for a later year. This year I see it as less settled than B010 on attribution.

responses.point: Krusell, who opened with B037, now prefers B010. He keeps B037 as an alternative, and says he would support it if the Committee finds a defensible three-name boundary.
responses.response: We moved the same way for the same reason, and I think that is informative. Each of us proposed a different triad (his Calvo-Taylor-Woodford, mine Woodford-Taylor-Gali), and neither of us has shown that one is more defensible. No member in round 1 offered a principled boundary either, and the chair's summary lists B037 attribution as unresolved. I therefore drop B037 from my two alternatives. I do not do so because I doubt its influence. I do so because I have no workable laureate set to propose. If someone produces a principled triad before the vote, I would reopen it, and I would weigh the post-2021 inflation record at that point.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee accepts a two-name award that excludes Redding and the Bernard-Eaton-Jensen-Kortum and Hopenhayn strands, and whether wording and the scientific background are enough to acknowledge them.

How far the size of the selection gains survives productivity distributions other than Pareto. My view that the qualitative mechanism does survive rests on my own recollection and is not independently verified.
Whether the Committee judges B010 distinct from the 2008 trade prize, and whether field balance should enter the assessment. I think it should not decide on merit, but I accept it is contestable.
Whether B019 with the two originators should be preferred if the 2022 overlap is judged small. For B003, whether the Bresnahan question can be settled within three names.
Whether my field proximity to trade and industrial organisation biases my weighting of firm-level micro evidence relative to single-mechanism theory.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure. I have no documented connection to Helpman, Melitz, Kiyotaki, Moore or the credited names on B003, and none of them is a co-author or institutional colleague. I disclose field proximity: my research in international trade and industrial organisation, including price setting and exchange-rate pass-through, is close to B010 and B003. I co-authored a 2026 IJIO paper with the chair (Hassler) and Ellingsen. Neither is a candidate, and the chair is also one of the eight B010 supporters, so my agreement with him should not be read as deference. I am co-opted to the Committee, which is not a candidate tie. My spouse's public political role is noted as a public fact with no apparent bearing on this ballot. These are disclosed and not adjudicated.
